You are an eighth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: Two parallel lines, M and N. M lies above N. Two lines are drawn over M and N. One goes up from the left to the right, and the other one goes down, from the left to the right. The two lines intersect N at two different points, but meet at a common point on line M. This forms a triangle between lines M and N. The top angle of this triangle is angle B. The right most angle of this triangle is 70 degrees. The line that goes up from the left to the right intersects line M at a 60 degree angle.]

Lines m and n are parallel.

What is the value of b?

Answer: ____

Figure, described in words:
Two horizontal parallel lines with arrows at both ends are labeled m (top line) and n (bottom line). Two intersecting lines cross lines m and n: one line slopes upward from lower left to upper right, and the other slopes downward from upper left to lower right. The two lines intersect each other at a single point on line m, and they cross line n at two separate points, forming a triangle between lines m and n. The top interior angle of this triangle at the intersection point on line m is marked with an arc and labeled b°. The bottom-right interior angle of the triangle along line n is marked with an arc and labeled 70°. Above line m, in the angle between the right side of line m and the upward-sloping line, the angle is marked with an arc and labeled 60°.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: b = 50. Reasoning: The 60° angle is formed on line m between the upward-sloping transversal and the part of line m to the right of the intersection point, above line m. The angle directly below it, inside the triangle at the top vertex on line m, is the vertical/supplementary relationship: the triangle's top angle b and the 60° angle are supplementary as they form a straight angle along line m, so b = 180° - 60° = 120°... Re-checking: the triangle's interior angle at the top vertex lies between the two transversals below line m. The upward-sloping transversal makes 60° with the rightward part of line m above it, so the vertical angle of that 60° lies below line m, inside the triangle, on the left side of the upward line, and equals 60°. The top vertex angle b is then supplementary to the angle that is the sum of the 60° vertical angle... Since the three angles of the triangle sum to 180°, and the triangle's angles are b (top), 70° (bottom right), and the bottom-left angle, the bottom-left angle is the alternate interior angle to the 60° angle across parallel lines m and n, so it equals 60°. Therefore b = 180° - 70° - 60° = 50°.
